learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, which enables them to learn new methods and theories, and provides them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Basic knowledge about the use and programming of computers, operating systems, databases, and computer programs with application in engineering.
Adopt a responsible, orderly attitude to work and be willing to learn, considering the challenge posed by the necessary continuous training.
Work effectively in groups, integrating abilities and knowledge to make decisions in the field of industrial engineering.

syllabus_topics: Data: variables, constants, operators, expressions, and Data Structures.
Integrated Development Environments for C programming: Eclipse, Dev-C++, NetBeans...
Initial concepts: variables, constants, operators, expressions, data types, basic statements and I/O instructions.
assessment_rules: For continuous assessment, the written exam accounts for 60% and laboratory deliverables for 40% of the final grade. To incorporate the continuous assessment score, a minimum of 2 points (out of 6) must be obtained on the written exam. Students can renounce continuous assessment; in this case, 100% of the grade is determined by a single final exam (70% main part, 30% extra exercise). In the extraordinary call, students may choose to keep the 40% continuous assessment score from the ordinary call, provided they met the minimum written exam score. Otherwise, they can take a comprehensive exam covering 100% of the grade, structured similar to the renunciation option. Non-appearance for an exam results in a "Not Presented" grade.
